items.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

ctx.x: Oh that’s interesting. Can we talk about how you got into education?

Well I used to teach a couple of blind students when I was in college and after a while my — let’s see I graduated, at the time I graduated I didn’t have a teaching credential, I received my B.S. in social sciences, so I had to go back to get the credential at USC. But then my oldest son, Charles Meeks, used to say, “Mother, I’m tired of going to Nanna’s” you know, when I’d go away to play. And one day that just stuck with me, I’ve got to be home now with these guys, the two of them. So then I started teaching.…
He wanted you to be there.
